gold_candidate.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
for: bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve, more extensive on the right
iris heterochromia with diffuse hyperpigmentation and evenly distributed micronodular elevations on the iris surface
increased retinal vessel tortuosity and a diffusely darker fundus in the right eye
A 12-year-old boy was referred for evaluation of a facial angioma
Gonioscopy demonstrated open angles bilaterally with diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye
against: MRI of the brain showed no leptomeningeal vascular malformations
